In \(\square\)WXYZ, \(\angle XWZ\) and \(\angle XYZ\) are opposite angles, and the opposite angles of a parallelogram are congruent.
So \(\angle XWZ = \angle XYZ = 135^{\circ}\).
\(\angle YZW\) is adjacent to \(\angle XYZ\), and adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary.
So \(\angle YZW = 180^{\circ} - 135^{\circ} = 45^{\circ}\).
The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so O is the midpoint of diagonal WY.
\(l(WY) = 2 \times l(OY) = 2 \times 5 = 10\) cm.
Hence \(\angle XWZ = 135^{\circ}\), \(\angle YZW = 45^{\circ}\) and \(l(WY) = 10\) cm.

[Textbook misprint: the book's printed answer block gives \(x = 40^{\circ}\), attaching a degree sign to \(x\) itself. The value \(40\) is correct, but the unit is not: the stem defines \(\angle A = (3x + 12)^{\circ}\), so the degree sign already sits outside the bracket and \(x\) is a pure number. Writing \(x = 40^{\circ}\) would make \(\angle A = (3 \times 40^{\circ} + 12)^{\circ}\), which is not a measure of anything. The two angle answers in the same entry, \(\angle C = 132^{\circ}\) and \(\angle D = 48^{\circ}\), are correct as printed.]

\(\angle A\) and \(\angle B\) are adjacent angles of parallelogram ABCD, so they are supplementary.
\((3x + 12) + (2x - 32) = 180\)
\(5x - 20 = 180\), so \(5x = 200\) and \(x = 40\).
So \(\angle A = (3 \times 40 + 12)^{\circ} = 132^{\circ}\) and \(\angle B = (2 \times 40 - 32)^{\circ} = 48^{\circ}\).
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are congruent, so \(\angle C = \angle A\) and \(\angle D = \angle B\).
Hence \(x = 40\), \(\angle C = 132^{\circ}\) and \(\angle D = 48^{\circ}\).

Let the smaller side be \(x\) cm; the other side is \((x + 25)\) cm.
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent, so the perimeter is \(2\big(x + (x + 25)\big)\).
\(2(2x + 25) = 150\), so \(2x + 25 = 75\), \(2x = 50\) and \(x = 25\).
So the sides are \(25\) cm and \(25 + 25 = 50\) cm.
Hence the four sides measure 25 cm, 50 cm, 25 cm and 50 cm.

Let the two adjacent angles be \(x^{\circ}\) and \(2x^{\circ}\).
Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary, so \(x + 2x = 180\), giving \(3x = 180\) and \(x = 60\).
So the adjacent angles are \(60^{\circ}\) and \(120^{\circ}\).
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are congruent, so the remaining two angles are \(60^{\circ}\) and \(120^{\circ}\) as well.
Hence the four angles measure \(60^{\circ}\), \(120^{\circ}\), \(60^{\circ}\) and \(120^{\circ}\).

In \(\triangle\)AOB, \(AO = 5\), \(BO = 12\) and \(AB = 13\).
\(AO^2 + BO^2 = 5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169\) and \(AB^2 = 13^2 = 169\).
So \(AO^2 + BO^2 = AB^2\), and by the converse of Pythagoras' theorem \(\angle AOB = 90^{\circ}\).
So the diagonals AC and BD of parallelogram ABCD are perpendicular to each other.
A parallelogram whose diagonals are perpendicular is a rhombus.
Hence \(\square\)ABCD is a rhombus.

In \(\square\)PQRS, \(\angle P\) and \(\angle R\) are opposite angles, so \(\angle R = \angle P = 110^{\circ}\).
Side AR lies along side SR and side CR lies along side QR, so \(\angle ARC\) is the same angle as \(\angle SRQ\).
So in \(\square\)ABCR, \(\angle ARC = 110^{\circ}\).
Opposite angles of parallelogram ABCR are congruent, so \(\angle ABC = \angle ARC = 110^{\circ}\).
Adjacent angles are supplementary, so \(\angle RAB = \angle BCR = 180^{\circ} - 110^{\circ} = 70^{\circ}\).
Hence \(\angle RAB = 70^{\circ}\), \(\angle ABC = 110^{\circ}\), \(\angle BCR = 70^{\circ}\) and \(\angle ARC = 110^{\circ}\).

\(\square\)ABCD is a parallelogram, so side DC \(\parallel\) side AB and \(DC = AB\).
Point E is on ray AB, so seg BE lies along line AB, and therefore seg BE \(\parallel\) seg DC.
Also \(BE = AB = DC\).
So in \(\square\)BECD the opposite sides BE and DC are parallel and congruent, and by the test for a parallelogram \(\square\)BECD is a parallelogram.
The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and the diagonals of \(\square\)BECD are seg BC and seg ED, which meet at F.
So F is the midpoint of seg BC.
Hence line ED bisects seg BC at point F.
